refnamediv.refpurpose: Report size and free disk space of mounted file systems as system report metrics

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: systemd-report-diskspace@.service is a metrics source for systemd-report1. It reports the size of the mounted file systems and how much disk space is still available on them, by implementing the io.systemd.Metrics Varlink interface on a socket linked into the /run/systemd/report/ directory.

All mount points of the system are enumerated. Mount points of file systems that are not backed by a block device (i.e. pseudo file systems such as proc, sysfs or tmpfs, network file systems, overlay, …) are skipped, as are read-only mount points. For each remaining mount point two gauge metrics are reported, with the mount point path as metric object:

listitem.para: The total size of the file system, in bytes. This matches the 1K-blocks column of df1 (scaled to bytes).

The disk space still available to unprivileged users on the file system, in bytes. This matches the Avail column of df1, i.e. space reserved for the superuser (as many file systems do) is not counted as free.

refsect1.para: The following metric fields are set on both metrics:

listitem.para: The file system type, for example ext4 or btrfs. Always set.
The mount source, typically the device node the file system is mounted from, for example /dev/sda1. Omitted if unknown.

If the block device the file system is mounted from is a stacked one (for example a LUKS or other device mapper volume), the device node of the block device it ultimately originates from, for example /dev/sda2 for a file system mounted from /dev/mapper/root. Omitted if the source is not a stacked block device, or its origin cannot be determined.

refsect1.para: A file system that is mounted multiple times (for example via bind mounts, or as multiple subvolumes of the same volume) is reported only once, under the shortest of its mount point paths (and among equally long ones, the alphabetically first). Mount points that are shadowed by another mount on top of them, or that the service cannot access, are not considered.
